scene_translation: The man disappeared into the dim alley behind the shrine as though swallowed by shadow, never once looking back. When the player turned the corner, he was standing there, leaning against the wall, watching — as if he had been waiting all along. "You are Tesuto-san," the man said quietly. "Your grandmother had spoken to me about you." From the breast pocket of his grey suit, he withdrew a folded piece of paper and pressed it into the player's hand.
grammar_note: 【まるで〜かのように】'as if / just as though' — a vivid simile construction. まるで待っていたかのように = 'as if he had been waiting.' The かの adds a slightly literary, distancing nuance compared to plain ように alone. Also note the man's speech: 伺っておりました uses おります, the humble-respectful (謙譲語) form of います — a register marker of formal, careful politeness, implying he is someone who deals with people of standing.

mystery_memo: The grey-suited man — now confirmed as an agent or associate connected to the player's deceased grandmother — has made direct contact. He knew the player's name unprompted (echoing the hook from Scene 1), deepening the central mystery of how the grandmother's world intersects with the player's present. The folded paper likely contains information related to the underground passages sketched in the notebook. The man's tone is formal and non-threatening but guarded; relationship status: neutral-formal, intent unknown. The old shopkeeper remains too frightened to be useful for now. Next: the man should ask or reveal something that requires the player to respond — perhaps asking whether the player has opened the coin locker, or what they know about the notebook, forcing the player to decide how much to trust him.
